genericProblem: A database-backed integration test can fail before its intended assertion when its fixture helper treats a database-constrained or content-addressed persisted value as arbitrary decoration. Such a failure neither disproves production behavior nor supplies focused proof.

finiteDenominator.invariant: staged asset storage keys are content-addressed and unique, so two distinct logical staged assets cannot use identical bytes
organization.head_company.credit_code is nonblank, unique per workspace/key, and limited to varchar(32)

findings.finding: The batch asset test stages two byte-identical 1x1 PNGs. Their shared content digest produces the same storage key and violates staged_asset_storage_key_key before the batch owner read can be tested.

The head-company test helper derives credit_code by appending '-credit' to a human-readable code. One valid descriptive test code becomes 34 characters and violates the real varchar(32) persistence constraint.

counterexamples: Production content-addressed storage uniqueness is required behavior and must not be weakened for a test.
Human-readable organization code may remain longer than a derived credit-code limit when the fixture generates the constrained field independently.
A fixture-only repair does not change public contract, owner authority, database schema or CRUD efficiency claim.
minimalReusableFix: Fixture helpers must generate distinct valid content for distinct logical immutable assets and must derive constrained persisted identifiers from a bounded unique source instead of concatenating display-oriented labels.

preventionDispositions.owningSourceOrControl: C13 focused-test review: immutable content fixtures must be distinct whenever the scenario models distinct staged objects
C13 focused-test review: each SQL fixture field must satisfy its actual schema length, uniqueness and nonblank constraints
